page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with a running head and page number at the top; a catchword at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: ctrina, tanta inest tibi pietas, perlegi volumen eruditione refertum, & eloquentiæ Gallicæ luminibus & Pigmentis respersum atque illustratum omnibus, paucos, veniam dabis amico candido, & libertate Gallica tecum agenti, nævos eximendos reperi, & adnotavi, pressique, & premo me penes, mox in sinum effusurus tuum, nam internos ex formula fiduciæ cuncta geri, & inter bonos bene agier oporteret: interim gratias habeo ingentes pro indice Ecclesiasticarum exercitationum ad Samaritanum Pentateuchum, qui tui in me benevoli animi & ingenii in sacris historiis, librisque versatissimi fidissimus, & certissimus index est, mox relaturus pro ipsis Exercitationibus, quas Goezellus à te missus pollicitus est, eas ego jam legi apud eminentissimum Cardinalem Mecœnatem meum, & collaudavi uti decebat. Sed vidist in[?] illud Tertuliani fragmentum cum Donationis charta, quæ typis etiam Lutetiæ fuêre mandata? cum à me prius Roma fuissent in lucem edita, tuam ego de[?]

page.notes: A printed brace stands in the right margin beside the line "Ecclesiasticarum" (lines 12–13); it is a mark, not text. The word "ctrina" at the head of the first line is cut at the page edge; its first letter is not clear, so it is given as printed with the fragment kept. The superscript mark after "in" in "vidist in" is unclear. The catchword is read as "ds", probably "de", and is uncertain.
